page: Microsoft Azure E64a_v4 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine in the EAv4 series, hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor operating at 3.525 GHz, delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture provides 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Instruction set flags include AVX, AES, and SHA_NI, with no AVX-512 support. Hardware provisioning includes 512 GB of system RAM, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 1,718 GB of local SSD temporary storage and zero dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallelized processing and memory capability. The server records upper-tier scores in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 260.47 GB/sec, PassMark CPU testing at 52,454.92, PassMark encryption at 63,026.07, and PassMark memory operations at 2,843.71. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 106.39 GB/sec alongside 52.53 GB/sec write bandwidth. A primary performance tradeoff is single-core throughput; single-threaded stress-ng scores rank in the lower percentiles. Similarly, LLM inference text generation on a 7B parameter model achieves 5.31 tokens/sec, reflecting the architectural limitations of running dense vector models without dedicated hardware accelerators or AVX-512 extensions.

In terms of qualitative cost efficiency, the E64a_v4 consolidates high memory density and 64 dedicated compute threads with bundled local SSD capacity into a single instance, eliminating the need to pay for unneeded GPU hardware. This resource profile fits workloads where memory capacity and multi-threaded scaling take precedence over single-threaded clock speed. Recommended use cases include large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers such as Redis, enterprise relational database servers, extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines, and memory-intensive data analytics.
description: Microsoft Azure E64a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, driven by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor running at 3.525 GHz on x86_64 architecture. The server is provisioned with 512 GB of system memory, achieving an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, coupled with 1,718 GB of local SSD storage and no GPUs. Benchmark metrics show strong marks in PassMark CPU performance, multi-threaded decompression, PassMark memory bandwidth, and AES-accelerated encryption. Conversely, single-core stress-ng tests and complex language model generation metrics demonstrate average to poor performance, emphasizing an architecture optimized for multi-threaded concurrency rather than individual core speed. By coupling substantial RAM with fast local storage, the instance delivers high resource density for memory-bound applications. It is appropriate for large-scale in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, high-concurrency web backends, and distributed big data batch processing.
